content_list.content_text: In 1989, film production in Britain was at a low ebb. Audience numbers were starting to grow, but few British films enjoyed commercial success. Yet the talent of British actors remained in evidence, and Daniel Day-Lewis (b. 1957) greeted the new decade by winning the Oscar for Best Actor for his performance as Christy Brown in My Left Foot: The Story of Christy Brown (1989).

information.contentTitle: Scenes from Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels
information.contentText: The film brought Ritchie international acclaim and introduced actors Jones, a former Wales international footballer, and Jason Statham, a former diver, to audiences worldwide.

content_list.content_text: Fifteen British and Irish actors received Oscar nominations for Best Actor or Actress in the 1990s, and their success kept Anglo-Irish cinema in the spotlight. The decade saw the passing of one of Britain's most innovative directors, Derek Jarman (1942-1994), but new talents burst onto the scene, such as Danny Boyle (b. 1956), with the wry Shallow Grave (1994) and Trainspotting (1996). Guy Ritchie (b. 1968) reinvigorated the gangster film with his black comedy about cockney criminals, Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels (1998).

Meanwhile, Mike Leigh (b. 1943) consolidated his position as a major director with three internationally acclaimed films - Life Is Sweet (1990), Naked (1993) and Secrets & Lies (1996). The last of these charted new territory by examining racial barriers and stereotypes, reflecting a contemporary Britain trying to integrate an increasingly multiethnic identity.

information.contentText: Leigh drew on "people close to him who had experiences related to adoption" to make a film on the subject. Speaking about it, he said: "For years I had wanted to make a film that explored this situation in a fictional way. I also wanted to make a film about the new generation of young Black people who are moving forward, away from the ghetto stereotypes. And those were the starting points for a film that ended up being an exploration of roots and identity."

content_list.content_text: The British said goodbye to Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher in 1990, but Anglo-Irish films continued to reflect her philosophy. Neil Jordan (b. 1950), with The Crying Game (1992), and Jim Sheridan (b. 1949), with In the Name of the Father (1993), explored the effects of the Irish question and gave the conflict a human face.

quote.quote: People think it's all about misery and desperation and death... but what they forget is the pleasure of it.
quote.author: Renton (Ewan McGregor) in Trainspotting

content_list.content_text: Sheridan's film was based on the true story of the Guildford Four, who were wrongly accused of taking part in an IRA pub bombing. Daniel Day-Lewis plays one of the accused, Gerry Conlon, and the story centers on his relationship with his father, Giuseppe (Pete Postlethwaite), who was also imprisoned, and with his lawyer, Gareth Peirce (Emma Thompson). The lead actors earned Oscar nominations for their performances - the rebellious son, the humble father and the fighting lawyer made the film deeply moving. Directed by Ken Loach (b. 1936), Land and Freedom (1995) explores similar themes of identity and idealism against the backdrop of the Spanish Civil War.

information.contentTitle: Scenes from Four Weddings and a Funeral
information.contentText: Screenwriter Richard Curtis's own experiences as a wedding guest inspired the film's premise. According to Curtis, he started writing the screenplay at 34, after realizing he had attended more than 65 weddings over an 11-year period. At one wedding, he was propositioned by a fellow guest, but he turned her down and regretted it forever; as a result, he based the origin of Charles and Carrie's romance on that situation.

content_list.content_text: Although period dramas such as Howards End (1992) and Shakespeare in Love (1998) showed that they were still Britain's strong suit, the most gratifying development of the decade was the resurgence in popularity of homegrown comedy. The romantic comedy Four Weddings and a Funeral (1994), directed by Mike Newell (b. 1942), was a huge hit and launched the collaboration between screenwriter Richard Curtis (b. 1956) and actor Hugh Grant (b. 1960), which produced another hit five years later, Notting Hill (1999).

Grant's knack for portraying the bumbling but attractive middle-class bachelor struck a chord with audiences around the world, even if this English stereotype did not always seem familiar to local viewers. The success of Four Weddings and a Funeral paved the way for more authentic British productions such as Brassed Off (1996) and The Full Monty (1997), which showed working-class people who might be down but did not feel defeated.

information.contentText: The film caused controversy in some countries, including the United Kingdom and the United States, over claims that it promoted drug use. U.S. Senator Bob Dole harshly criticized it during the 1996 presidential campaign, despite admitting that he had never actually seen the film.

content_list.content_text: The resistance of the brass band members in Brassed Off to the closure of their rehearsal space, and of the unemployed men in The Full Monty who become strippers, appealed to international audiences, showing that Anglo-Irish filmmakers did not need to dilute their own culture to suit American tastes.

movies.title: Trainspotting
movies.overview: Heroin addict Mark Renton stumbles through bad ideas and sobriety attempts with his unreliable friends -- Sick Boy, Begbie, Spud and Tommy. He also has an underage girlfriend, Diane, along for the ride. After cleaning up and moving from Edinburgh to London, Mark finds he can't escape the life he left behind when Begbie shows up at his front door on the lam, and a scheming Sick Boy follows.

movies.title: Four Weddings and a Funeral
movies.overview: Over the course of five social occasions, a committed bachelor must consider the notion that he may have discovered love.

movies.title: Shattered
movies.overview: Shattered is a story based on true events about family betrayal, love lost, and a dark destructive secret that swirls around a high powered political family in the Deep South. Kate Stenson dreams of an enviable life as the quintessential Southern Belle. She marries Ken Burnett, the son of the town's powerful Mayor - a controlling father who will do anything to protect his position. Kate has two children with Ken - a biological daughter, and an adopted son, named Logan (Tate Birchmore). But Kate's seemingly perfect lifestyle begins to fray at the edges as she discovers that Logan suffers from severe mental health issues. Kate's journey to uncover the true story of Logan's past reveals a dark secret that can destroy the entire Burnett legacy. As Kate investigates - with the aid of a new friend - to unmask the history behind Logan's illness, these unimaginable family secrets surface, putting her in unforeseen danger.

movies.title: The Crying Game
movies.overview: Irish Republican Army member Fergus forms an unexpected bond with Jody, a kidnapped British soldier in his custody, despite the warnings of fellow IRA members Jude and Maguire. Jody makes Fergus promise he'll visit his girlfriend, Dil, in London, and when Fergus flees to the city, he seeks her out. Hounded by his former IRA colleagues, he finds himself increasingly drawn to the enigmatic, and surprising, Dil.

movies.title: Howards End
movies.overview: A saga of class relations and changing times in an Edwardian England on the brink of modernity, the film centers on liberal Margaret Schlegel, who, along with her sister Helen, becomes involved with two couples: wealthy, conservative industrialist Henry Wilcox and his wife Ruth, and the downwardly mobile working-class Leonard Bast and his mistress Jackie.

movies.title: The Madness of King George
movies.overview: King George III's erratic behaviour leads to a plot in Parliament to have him declared insane and removed from the throne.

movies.title: Sense and Sensibility
movies.overview: Rich Mr. Dashwood dies, leaving his second wife and her daughters poor by the rules of inheritance. Two daughters are the titular opposites.

movies.title: Mrs Brown
movies.overview: When Queen Victoria's husband Prince Albert dies, she finds solace in her trusted servant, Mr. John Brown. But their relationship also brings scandal and turmoil to the monarchy.

movies.title: The Full Monty
movies.overview: Sheffield, England. Gaz, a jobless steelworker in need of quick cash persuades his mates to bare it all in a one-night-only strip show.

movies.title: My Left Foot: The Story of Christy Brown
movies.original_title: My Left Foot: The Story of Christy Brown
movies.overview: In this true story told through flashbacks, Christy Brown is born with crippling cerebral palsy into a poor, working-class Irish family. Able only to control movement in his left foot and to speak in guttural sounds, he is mistakenly believed to have a intellectual disability for the first ten years of his life.
